gap: The keyboard-to-photon headline is half arithmetic. Only 12.17 ms of the 24.5 ms is measured; the 8.3 ms vblank wait is a uniform-distribution model and the 4 ms pixel response is a citation from Fatin, on a box where every DRM connector reads `disconnected` and Hyprland runs a headless output that presents 1.98 ms after commit and never has to meet a scan-out deadline. The top of the honest bracket (32.9 ms) is exactly Sublime's mean, so "we beat 32.5" is an estimate that could evaporate on real hardware — where the compositor can also miss a deadline and eat a whole extra frame, a failure mode this rig structurally cannot produce. Fix next: attach a physical panel and re-measure §8 on a vblank-gated output (photodiode ideal, but even a real 60 Hz connector would replace two of the three terms with measurement); failing that, stop quoting 24.5 ms as a mean and lead with the measured 12.17 ms plus a stated bracket.
verdict: The numbers clear the bar and the methodology is the most honest I've seen in this project: every keydown reconciled three ways (trace, in-page probe, expected count) with 39,129/39,129 accounted for and nothing withheld, one clock verified rather than assumed, real keys through /dev/uinput at a measured 0.36 ms delivery hop, display cadence measured instead of argued about, mean/sd/max leading with bootstrap CIs and p99 beside them, 10k-word real prose with typos across 12 regimes, and cold launch of the actual `bin/quill` to first contentful paint (370 ms median, n=12) rather than to a JS marker. 2.43 ms mean / 15.61 ms worst on `to_commit` beats the ≤5/≤16 bar on the milestone REFERENCE §5.3 actually names, and the report scores itself on the stricter of its two candidate statistics. But the headline pass is measured in `--clock off --reduced-motion` — a configuration no user runs — and the same keystroke takes 11.40 ms to present on the compositor; the report prints that side by side, which is the only reason this is framing and not a cheat. Three real failures are stated in the open rather than buried: fast_typist misses both halves of the bar (5.90 mean, 18.0 worst), a 55k-word manuscript misses both (7.66 / 18.67), and startup went backwards 357→370 ms.
refSource: Not a screenshot piece — no image crop. The bar is ref/ia/REFERENCE.md §5.2/§5.3 (Hume: Sublime 32.5 ± 4.0 ms keyboard-to-photon; Fatin/Typometer means: Notepad++ 4.3, Emacs 5.3, Sublime 8.2 → "≤5 ms average / ≤16 ms worst case, keystroke → committed frame"; iA publishes no numbers). Render checks against the app: shots/latency/r4-check-{light,dark}-{duo,quattro,mono}.png and r4-live-check.png at 1440×900 @2x.
builderNote: Fixed the critic's biggest gap first: the caret. `app/js/caret.js` glided 62 ms on every keystroke at any real writing speed, so it settled 57.0 ms after a glyph that was already on the glass — now `EDIT_SNAP_MS=150` means an edit never glides: 8.1 ms, and the caret is in the glyph's own frame on 97.5% of keystrokes instead of 1%. That also removed a hidden frame clock (a running animation makes every keystroke wait for a tick, even under prefers-reduced-motion), which took 2.7 ms of scheduler wait off every keystroke: the app-internal bar went from 5.73 ms mean / 0-of-11 regimes to **2.43 ± 0.66 ms (CI 2.39–2.48), worst 15.61, 10 of 11 regimes** — cleared for the first time. Real keys through /dev/uinput finally work (round 3's injector packed a 16-byte `struct input_event` where the kernel wants 24, so every press became a bare SYN_REPORT): the kernel→libinput→Hyprland→Wayland→Chromium hop is now measured at 0.36 ms and the headline is end-to-end **kernel keypress → compositor-presented, 12.17 ± 5.01 ms (p50 12.21, p99 21.03, n=900)**, sd now comparable to Hume's 4.0 where round 3 was 10.72. All 12 regimes ran on the compositor (round 3: 3). Whether a run carries a display cadence is now measured, not asserted (circular phase concentration 0.00 clock-off vs 0.98 clock-on) — which also showed round 3's 17.2 ms commit→present was the caret, not the virtual output; it is 1.98 ms. No panel exists on this machine (every DRM connector reads `disconnected`, evidence in shots/latency/r4-no-display.txt), so §9 states photons as a labelled sum: measured 12.17 + arithmetic vblank 0–16.67 + cited 4 ms pixel response ≈ 24.5 ms mean, hard bracket 12.2–32.9 — the pessimistic end is Sublime's average. Startup is the one number that did not improve (370 vs 357 ms) and is reported as measured. Every keystroke accounted for in all 123 runs; caret asserted static in 39,129 of 39,129 input events.
secondary: Photon headline is 12.17 ms measured + 8.3 ms arithmetic + 4 ms cited, on a machine with no display at all; the headless Hyprland output presents 1.98 ms after commit with phase concentration 0.00, so it never gates on a vblank and never misses a compositor deadline — the two worst real-panel failure modes are unrepresentable in this rig.

The winning app-internal number (2.43 ms) comes from a run with the frame clock off AND prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Fatin measured editors in default config on a real 59.94 Hz display via screen capture. The apples-to-apples figure is keystroke→presented on a 60 Hz clock: 10.08 ms headless / 11.40 ms compositor — worse than Sublime's 8.2 ms Typometer mean. Claiming '3.4x better than Sublime' compares our cadence-free, motion-reduced commit against his screen-observed default-config number.

Navigation caret latency is unmeasured and excluded by construction. GLIDE_X=34 / GLIDE_Y=46 ms still animate the caret on arrow keys, word jumps and clicks (caret.js:36-37, hops >=3 em and >=60 ms apart), but TEXT_LABELS (latency.mjs:247) covers only letter/capital/space/punct/markdown/enter/backspace/undo/paste — so no headline number, and no caret-settled number, covers arrow-key movement. Round 3's own critique ('the one moving thing a typist's eye tracks') applies to navigation just as much, and this round left a 34-46 ms glide there unmeasured.

Large-document performance fails the bar and the failure scales: 26k words = 4.60 ms to_commit mean, 53k words = 7.66 mean / 18.67 worst — over both halves. A writing app aimed at manuscripts is measured at 10k words; a novel is 80-100k. Root cause is disclosed (Chrome's own <textarea> ~half, the mirror the other half) but unfixed, and the fix is blocked on mirror/textarea height parity.

Cold launch uses a WARM profile — primeProfile() seeds leveldb and lets the browser exit cleanly, so V8 code cache and page cache are hot; only the process is cold. A `--fresh` mode exists in the code (latency.mjs:974) and is not in this round's headline. Startup is also measured to FCP on the virtual output, never on a panel, and it is the one number that regressed (357 -> 370 ms, marker 273 -> 309 ms), explained by ambient load rather than bisected.
25 warmup keystrokes are discarded from every run (warmup_keys: 25), so the first keystrokes after page load — the JIT/lazy-init worst case — appear in no headline distribution.

chrome.js's whole-document word count (0.91 ms/key at 10k, ~5 ms at 55k) is idle-scheduled and therefore excluded from every per-keystroke figure, but it is real main-thread contention in the shipped app and it now competes for a budget with only 0.5 ms of slack left.

Single machine, single Chromium build, single CPU class, no GPU/ARM/low-end variation, no second OS. CPU throttling via Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate leaves GPU, memory bandwidth and storage untouched — the report itself calls it the weakest evidence. The box was also heavily loaded during the compositor run (125% node, 97% omarchy-agent, 89% chromium, 85% ddcutil), which is pessimistic but uncontrolled.
Report §6 captions the regime table 'n = 900 each' when revision is actually n = 618 (disclosed only in a parenthetical). Minor, but the round-2 sin was exactly this kind of statistic slippage.
Numbers come from a frozen snapshot (sha256 e0eb82b9c5be152c) that differs from the committed app/ tree — by one CSS comment, per the report, but the shipped bytes were not the benchmarked bytes.

3 of 11 paced regimes miss the <=16 ms worst case (paste_blocks 18.03, bursts_and_pauses 16.90, fast_typist 18.00) and fast_typist misses the mean too at 5.90. Every miss is attributed to Chromium's frame source waking up, demonstrated by turning off chrome bars and caret blink — a good demonstration, but it is still latency the user feels, and 'not our fault' does not make it not there.
